newsitem.title: USA: Kmart says can add $8-$10 billion in sales.
newsitem.headline: Kmart says can add $8-$10 billion in sales.

text.p: Kmart Corp, which had more than $26 billion of revenue last year from its 2,038 traditional stores, said Tuesday it has the potential to grow sales another $8.0-$10.0 billion.

"We have the potential to grow our sales another $8 to $10 billion on this existing store base," said Chairman Floyd Hall. "That has encouraged us to refine and enthusiastically pursue the new store prototype -- which we call Big Kmart."

About 300 traditional Kmart stores have already been converted to the new prototype, which features design and other changes affecting 90 percent of the store. An additional 300 stores will be converted this year.

Kmart is on track to modify as many as 450 stores into this format annually for the next three years, upgrading about half the chain and driving improved volumes, Hall said. The company will spend about $270 million to convert stores in 1997, he added.

"Our experience indicates that the store conversion process provides Kmart with improved performance against new competition, so our ongoing roll-out will emphasize metropolitan areas such as the Northeast in which we anticipate increased competition over the next several years," Hall said in a presentation to shareholders.
He also said the retailer is in the early stages of a turnaround and must gain momentum that it can sustain.
"At the top of our agenda in 1997 is a tenacious push toward growing sales and improving profitability," Hall said.
Hall said the comapny plans a new Sesame Street line that will be introduced this summer, featuring clothing for infants, toddlers, boys and girls, as well as toys, books and related products.

"You will see a powerful product launch for this new line which we believe will go a very long way in building our relationship with families who want the very best for their children at a price they can afford," Hall said.

He said Kmart is rolling out a new "co-branded" program for its 850 in-store restaurants beginning this week. The new "KCafe" restaurants will have expanded menu offerings that feature national brands.

In the 530 Kmart stores that have a Little Caesars restaurant, the company will introduce a new format to be called "The KCafe/Little Caesars Pizza Station," which will offer the full new menu as well as fresh-made pizza.
The 320 other restaurants will be called "The KCafe/Little Caesars Express."
The company said it plans to incorporate the new KCafe in all of its high-frequency Big Kmart stores.
